about: Approximate positions for the Endurance / James Caird map. Coordinates are [lon, lat] in decimal degrees (WGS84, west and south negative). 'confidence' says how far to trust each point: 'recorded' = a position written down at the time (sextant/log) or a published survey fix; 'gazetteer' = a named place, position from a gazetteer / encyclopaedia; 'approx' = estimated by me from a description (good to a few km or worse); 'illustrative' = only to draw a plausible line, not a real fix.

sources.south: Shackleton, E. H. South: The Story of Shackleton's Last Expedition 1914-1917 (Heinemann, 1919). Project Gutenberg #5199: https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/5199/pg5199.txt
sources.ats_wp047: Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meeting XLIV, Working Paper 047 (UK and South Africa), 'Discovery of the wreck of Endurance - Updating information for HSM 93': https://documents.ats.aq/ATCM44/wp/ATCM44_wp047_e.docx

points.label: Grytviken, South Georgia: departure
points.quote: I gave the order to heave anchor at 8.45 a.m. on December 5, 1914, and the clanking of the windlass broke for us the last link with civilization. (South)

points.label: Endurance beset (frozen in), Weddell Sea
points.quote: Our position on the morning of the 19th was lat. 76° 34´ S., long. 31° 30´ W. ... The ice had closed around the ship during the night, and no water could be seen in any direction from the deck. (South)
points.conflict: South's scientific appendix gives the same latitude but long. 37° 30´ W ('held up in about lat. 76° 34´ S. and long. 37° 30´ W. on January 19, 1915'). The narrative (31° 30´ W) agrees with Wikipedia and with the reported net drift of 95 miles N 80° W by 31 March; 37° 30´ looks like a typo. Use 31° 30´ W.

points.label: Drift reaches about 77° S, then turns west and north
points.quote: The ship drifted to lat. 76° 59´ S., long. 37° 47´ W. on March 19, 1915, and then west and north until crushed in lat. 69° 5´ S. and long. 51° 30´ W. (South, appendix)

points.label: Ship crushed and abandoned
points.quote: Then came a fateful day—Wednesday, October 27. The position was lat. 69° 5´ S., long. 51° 30´ W. (South)

points.label: Endurance sinks: position as logged by Worsley
points.quote: November 21, 1915.—This evening, as we were lying in our tents we heard the Boss call out, 'She's going, boys!' (South). ATS WP047 lists Worsley's recorded position as 68° 39' 29.9987" S, 52° 26' 30" W.

points.label: Wreck found by Endurance22 (3,008 m deep)
points.quote: On 5 March 2022, the Endurance22 expedition found the Endurance at a depth of 3,008 metres in the Weddell Sea at location 68°44'21'' S, 52°19'47'' W (ATS WP047)
points.note: About 10 km (5.4 nmi) south-east of Worsley's logged position.

points.label: Patience Camp drifting north (level with Paulet Island)
points.quote: by 17 March, brought Patience Camp to the latitude of Paulet Island, but 60 nm (111 km) to its east (Wikipedia, ITAE)
points.note: Derived: Paulet Island is at about 63°35'S 55°47'W; 60 nmi east at that latitude is about 2.2° of longitude.

points.label: Ice breaks up; the three boats are launched
points.quote: ...finally took to the boats on April 9, 1916, and reached Elephant Island on April 15. (South, appendix)
points.note: No position for 9 April was found in South; this point only bridges Patience Camp and Elephant Island on the map.

points.label: First landing on Elephant Island, Cape Valentine
points.quote: The First Landing ever made on Elephant Island, April 15, 1916 (South, illustration caption); 'Rough sketch map of landing place and first camp at C. Valentine, Elephant Island' (South, list of illustrations)

points.label: Point Wild ('Cape Wild'): camp under the upturned boats
points.quote: Wild ... had discovered a sandy spit seven miles to the west, about 200 yds. long, running out at right angles to the coast ... The morning of April 17 came fine and clear. (South)

points.label: James Caird leaves Elephant Island (6 men)
points.quote: On April 25, the day after I left for South Georgia, the island was beset by heavy pack-ice (South)

points.label: James Caird lands at Cave Cove, King Haakon Bay
points.quote: We had sighted in the meantime a big indentation which I thought must be King Haakon Bay, and I decided that we must land there. (South); 'A noon observation on this day gave our latitude as 54° 10´ 47´´ S.' (South, written at Cave Cove)
points.note: Latitude from Worsley's noon sight at Cave Cove; longitude estimated at the mouth of King Haakon Bay (Wikipedia/GNIS gives the bay as 54°09'S 37°19'W).

points.label: Peggotty Camp, head of King Haakon Bay: start of the crossing
points.quote: King Haakon Bay is an eight-mile sound penetrating the coast of South Georgia in an easterly direction. (South); 'We turned out at 2 a.m. on the Friday morning and had our hoosh ready an hour later.' (South; that Friday was 19 May 1916)
points.note: Placed near the head of the bay on its north side, as described; uncertain to about ±5 km.

points.label: Stromness whaling station: end of the 36-hour crossing
points.quote: that long and racking march of thirty-six hours over the unnamed mountains and glaciers of South Georgia (South)

points.label: Yelcho (Capt. Luis Pardo) rescues the 22 men at Point Wild
points.quote: at 10 a.m. on August 30 we passed some stranded bergs. Then we saw the sea breaking on a reef, and I knew that we were just outside the island. (South)

points.label: Punta Arenas, Chile: rescued men arrive
points.quote: We entered the Straits of Magellan on September 3 and reached Rio Secco at 8 a.m. ... Two hours later we were at Punta Arenas (South)

lines.label: Endurance: Grytviken to the point where she was beset (simplified; she skirted the pack and the Coats Land coast)
lines.note: Waypoints between Grytviken and the beset point are only a sketch: South gives noon positions just before 21 December and on 24 December 1914 (lat. 62° 42´ S., long. 17° 54´ W. and lat. 64° 32´ S., long. 17° 17´ W.) at about 17-18° W, i.e. EAST of the 25° W map edge. Clip or drop this line if the map stops at 25° W.

lines.label: Endurance and the camps drifting with the ice
lines.note: Recorded points joined by a smooth guess; the real drift track zig-zagged. Fixes: beset, 19 Mar 1915, abandoned, sank (logged), Patience Camp (approx), Cape Valentine.

lines.label: Boats move from Cape Valentine to Point Wild (about 7 miles west)
James Caird: Point Wild to Cave Cove, 24 April - 10 May 1916
lines.note: Endpoints are real; the middle is a plausible line only (Shackleton first steered north to get clear of the ice, then north-east). Great-circle distance Point Wild to Cave Cove is about 1,290 km = 697 nmi = 802 statute miles, which matches Shackleton's 'over 800 miles' (statute miles), not 800 nautical miles.

lines.label: Shackleton, Worsley and Crean cross South Georgia, 19-20 May 1916
lines.note: Straight-ish sketch; the real route looped south-east over the Crean and Fortuna glaciers before descending to Fortuna Bay and Stromness.

lines.label: Yelcho: Punta Arenas to Elephant Island and back, 25 Aug - 3 Sep 1916
